g.text: The Moon rises later each night, yet corals keep starting about 1 h 53 after sunset, on almost any night of the month.
So after full moon, 88% of them start in the dark, before the Moon is up.
Spawning keeps to the Sun, whatever the Moon is doing
Each dot: one genus starting on one spawning night (327 exact evening starts, 172 spawning nights, 35 subsites). Lighter sky: more moonlight, meaning how full the Moon is times how high.
Starts vary 2.7 times less around sunset than around moonrise. Moon formulas agree with 12,897 NASA/JPL Horizons positions to 0.3°. Coral data: Baird et al. (2021).
